sections.title: Open Mic: Frontier-Pacing Protocols
paragraphs: Thank you, Eric. Yeah, if you we our next session is actually um kind of open mic about frontier pacing, and I think Ben Garfinkel's leading on that one, but yeah, I'm um maybe you can just kick us off with like 2 minutes and what you think frontier pacing should be like since you're talking about kill switches, which is kind of an adjacent topic.
Ooh, frontier pacing. [laughter] I mean, the public choice concern is here in spades.

Which is it's one way to view some of the criticisms of the good faith incentives of the massive massive corporations that are calling for the government needs to pace us. And so my concern is is the call for please regulate us. We've seen this from railroads to you know massive massive corporations across the course of the 20th century. This is not to argue that we don't have a safety concern which I I think is quite serious but nonetheless arguing that we therefore need government intervention to ameliorate that concern is not to me an unambiguously clear answer and it has really troubling implications for our access to models that are not centrally controlled.

Because then the argument becomes oh all of the unsafe stuff is happening with these open weight models. But I've already spoken for past my time. Thank you for giving me the two-minute segway Timber and I look forward to Venkat.

So, that's why I think it's kind of nonsensical. Uh but but that is a sidebar. Okay, so that's kind of my very muddy uh um explanation of a very muddy situation that's still evolving rapidly. But, I've concluded that actually what's happened, so this is my first attempt at sense making, what's happened is that what used to be um So, back back up a month, right? Data centers were the hot topic in the election cycle running up to November, right? It was bipartisan, Democrats and Republicans were both hearing all over America. So, this is going to be a very America-centric sort of like open mic spiel by me. But okay, so couple of months back data center politics was framing the mainstream, right?

What's happened in the last couple of weeks is I think two more dimensions have gotten added to it. Um the first is this a conversation that was kind of like a little subcultural culty thing has suddenly gone mainstream because that one guy left Anthropic and showed up on Anderson Cooper and a lot of other places. Bernie Sanders kind of like proposed a non-starter bill saying we must stop development on like self-improving models even though I think he has no idea what he's talking about. That's a non-starter but it's like you know brought the topic into the Overton window so to speak. And the stock market is kind of staying afloat on AI kind of like boom positivity but it's very fragile. A lot of people a crash might happen. So there's that happening. This is I think one cynical reason Trump is acting as he does. I don't think he has any idea what AI is, what effective altruism is or what the safety concerns are.
